content.text: Energy doesn't just sit in stores—it moves. Understanding how energy transfers between stores is essential for analysing any physical process, from boiling water to powering a city. There are four main pathways by which energy can be transferred.
Energy transfers describe HOW energy moves between stores. The four pathways are mechanical work, electrical work, heating, and radiation.
(or energy pathway) is the mechanism by which energy moves from one store to another.

Light from Sun, sound from speaker

Describe the energy transfers when a phone charges and then plays music.
Mains electricity → Electrical transfer → Chemical store (battery)
Chemical store (battery) → Electrical transfer → Kinetic store (speaker vibrating) → Sound waves (radiation transfer) → Kinetic store (eardrums moving)
A kettle heats water. Describe the energy transfers and identify the useful and wasted energy.
Electrical energy input → Heating → Thermal store (water)
Thermal energy in the water (makes it hot)
Thermal energy in the kettle body

content.text: Dissipated energy is not 'lost' or destroyed. It has been transferred to thermal energy stores in the surroundings where it is spread out and difficult to use again.
— Energy is never lost, only transferred to less useful stores (usually thermal in surroundings).
— Heating is a transfer mechanism. The store is thermal energy.
— Electrical work is a transfer pathway, not a store. Energy is stored in chemical, kinetic, or other stores.
— Sound is a transfer mechanism (radiation). When we hear sound, energy is transferred to kinetic energy of eardrums.
— All solids conduct (metals are just better at it).
Energy transfers via four main pathways: mechanical work, electrical work, heating, radiation
Temperature difference causes energy transfer (conduction, convection, radiation)
EM waves or sound waves carry energy
Energy is conserved: input = useful output + wasted
Wasted energy is usually dissipated as thermal energy to surroundings
